speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how long this painful ulcer on your leg has been present and if you have any underlying conditions like diabetes or poor circulation? I also need to know if the area is warm to the touch or if you have developed a fever.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the painful nature of the ulcer, I need to know if you have any current gastrointestinal symptoms like abdominal pain, diarrhea, or rectal bleeding. Also, have you noticed any joint pain or swelling in your knees or ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of an ant bite at the site, combined with your Crohn's disease and the painful, necrotic appearance of the ulcer, strongly suggests a phenomenon known as pathergy. I will request a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology shows neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
